While the bull cites a "turnaround," the company’s operating margin has actually collapsed to -94% in the TTM [E27] and worsened to -97% in the most recent quarter [E28], suggesting that recent sales gains are not translating into viable business economics. However, this lack of debt does not compensate for the fact that the company is burning cash, with negative operating and free cash flow of Rs -0.60 Cr as of March 2026 [E32, E33]. The bull interprets the 4.50x price-to-book ratio [E1, E52] as a signal of confidence, yet this valuation is fundamentally disconnected from the company’s negative ROE [E12, E26] and its inability to generate returns for shareholders [E23, E24, E25]. Finally, the bull’s focus on momentum [E43, E44] ignores the extreme risk profile, characterized by an annualized volatility of 427,464.1% [E46] and a Sharpe ratio of only 0.23 [E47], indicating that the recent price appreciation is driven by speculative instability rather than sustainable value creation.
